title: Meet the f-string
idea: An f-string lets you drop a variable's value right inside text using {curly braces}.

exercises.prompt: An f-string starts with a little f before the quote. What does it let you do?
options: Put a variable's value inside text using {braces}
exercises.explanation: Write f"..." and anything in {braces} is swapped for that variable's value. Cleaner than lots of + signs.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

name = "Mia"
print(f"Hello, {name}")
exercises.explanation: The {name} is replaced by its value, Mia. The f at the front turns on the braces.

exercises.prompt:
What is different about these two?

print("Hello, {name}")
print(f"Hello, {name}")
options: Without the f, the braces are shown as plain text; with the f, the value fills in
exercises.explanation: No f means the braces are just characters: Hello, {name}. The f makes them do their job.

exercises.prompt: Inside an f-string, the spaces and punctuation outside the braces are shown exactly as written.
exercises.explanation: Only the {braces} get swapped. Everything else — spaces, commas, letters — appears exactly.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

city = "Hanoi"
print(f"I live in {city}")
exercises.explanation: {city} becomes Hanoi. The spaces are already in the text, so you get: I live in Hanoi.

exercises.prompt:
Add the one letter that turns this into an f-string so {name} fills in.

print(____"Hi {name}")
exercises.explanation: The f right before the opening quote switches on the braces: f"Hi {name}".

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

name = "Mia"
print(f"{name}, welcome!")
exercises.explanation: The brace can come first too. {name} becomes Mia, then the rest follows: Mia, welcome!

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints: Hi Mia (using an f-string, name holds "Mia").
exercises.explanation: f"Hi {name}" puts the value of name right after 'Hi '. No + signs needed.

exercises.prompt:
Compare these two correct lines. What do they both show?

print("Hello, " + name)
print(f"Hello, {name}")
exercises.explanation: Same result, Hello, Mia. The f-string is just a tidier way to write the same join.

exercises.prompt: With an f-string you don't have to remember to add spaces between + signs.
exercises.explanation: You write the sentence normally and drop {values} where you want them. Fewer things to forget.
